rv.q: McAvoy’s performance is glorious, stage-owning yet generous.
Once again, Lloyd proves he has a nose for a triumphant theatrical reinvention.

Writers are fighters and the word is everything in this firecracker show about passion, rejection, and the crazy genius of the spoken word. The rapiers, intrigue and censorship of Cardinal Richelieu’s Paris, circa 1640, are modernised as razor-sharp banter about love, sex, and – nudge, wink – cultural appropriation.
It’s a thrilling, moving revival with McAvoy outstanding as a man torn in two.
It’s a daringly contemporary re-working which will be remembered for one of the most imposing performances of the decade.

cn.t: McAvoy delivers a phenomenal, career-defining performance in Lloyd's radically stripped-down, modernized production that ditches the nose and period trappings for contemporary dress and verse. Critics hail the daring reimagining as blistering and fiercely charismatic.
